impact:
Scope boundary declared explicitly in T-005 rather than silently left open (plan section 3.5).

T-005 validates that every waiver a comparison policy consumes names a published ALLOWLIST entry, and that each policy actually executes its replacement assertions (proved by mutation-killing every predicate). That covers ALLOWLIST-19, -22b and -23.

What it deliberately does NOT cover: entries asserted by tests that are not parity cases — ALLOWLIST-22a (the product-name spans, asserted by the reviewed shipped-help snapshot) being the live example. An earlier plan revision proposed classifying such entries "enforceable" by listing their asserting test NAMES. Review correctly rejected that: the existence of a test name is exactly the "code exists, therefore it ran" evidence this repo removed dual_run_only to escape. Naming it proves nothing.

Doing it properly needs a runner that REPORTS which allowlist IDs actually executed — a machine-readable assertion registry, where a test declares the ID it asserts and the runner emits the set that ran, so coverage is computed from execution rather than from prose.

Until that exists, ALLOWLIST-22a is documented as snapshot-asserted and is not machine-verified. That is a stated gap, not a claim of coverage. Related: ALLOWLIST entry 22 was split into 22a/22b during T-005 precisely so the documentation-only half could not shelter the enforced half.
resolution:
Shipped in 584c3c9. `npm run test:allowlist`, wired into `test:all`.

The issue asked for exactly one thing — "a runner that REPORTS which allowlist IDs actually executed... so coverage is computed from execution rather than from prose" — and refused the shortcut of listing asserting test NAMES. That is what landed.

WHAT LANDED:
- tests-ts/harness/allowlist-witness.mjs — witness(id, {source, subject}), called immediately AFTER an assertion succeeds. Validates the id against ALLOWLIST.md on every call, sink or not, so a typo fails in ordinary test runs too.
- scripts/allowlist-coverage.mjs — runs parity --final plus the snapshot test with a sink, collects what executed, compares against the declaration.
- tests/golden/allowlist-assertions.json — the declaration. Explicitly intent, not evidence.
- Witness call sites in tests-ts/parity.mjs (after a policy's differential returns) and tests-ts/help-snapshot.test.mjs (ALLOWLIST-22a).

ALLOWLIST-22a IS NOW MACHINE-VERIFIED. It has no parity case — the approved artifact is the shipped-help snapshot, not a comparison between two implementations — so it is witnessed directly by its two assertion sites. ALLOWLIST.md's block on it is rewritten: the old paragraph explaining why it could not be verified is replaced by a description of the mechanism that now verifies it.

All five published ids are covered by execution evidence, and the witnessed case sets match the counts ALLOWLIST.md publishes exactly: 14 -> 1, 19 -> 13, 22b -> 5, 23 -> 2, 22a -> 2 sites.

THE WITNESS RECORDS MORE THAN AN ID, because an id alone is not enough — each of these was a hole review found:
1. SOURCE (policy | test). An id declared policy-covered was otherwise satisfied by any ordinary test witnessing the same id, so the named mechanism could be gone entirely while coverage read green.
2. SUBJECT. The witnessed case SET is compared against the "Cases covered by" list ALLOWLIST.md publishes — not the count, since the right number of the wrong cases is what a registry copy-paste produces.
3. ASSERTION COUNT. "differential() returned" is evidence of INVOCATION, not of assertion: an empty policy body returns normally and would record full coverage. The shared comparison helpers now count, differential's count is read, and the harness refuses to witness a zero.
4. PER-SITE subjects for witness mode. 22a has two sites covering two different claims (every command row names the shipped program; the oracle's program name appears nowhere as a command). Requiring only "some witness for 22a" would let either be deleted while the other kept the entry looking covered. requiredSubjects now demands exact agreement.

Also: the mode vocabulary is closed (policy | witness | none). Previously a typo like "polcy" fell through every branch and passed on any witness at all. And the success message no longer claims "every declared id was witnessed", which would be false the moment a `none` entry exists.

SCOPE NOTE: 5 of the 24 allowlist entries carry formal [ALLOWLIST-n] ids; the other 19 are numbered prose entries without one. This system covers the 5 formal ids, which is the scope ISS-020 named (its live example was 22a). Adding ids to the remaining entries is a separate question about the document, not about evidence.

REVIEW (codex, request_changes) FOUND SIX HOLES — all fixed, each mutation-verified as firing:
mode typo rejected; one of 22a's two sites deleted while the other still witnesses (caught); 22a redeclared as policy-covered when only a test witnesses it (caught); witness mode with no requiredSubjects (caught); the assertion counters removed so policies witness without asserting (caught, per case); plus the summary-wording fix.

INCIDENTAL FIX: writing `dualRunOnly` in a code span in ALLOWLIST.md violated this repo's own convention that a retired field is named in plain prose only, and parity's "every pre-T-005 comparison flag is fully retired" check failed on it. The guard caught my documentation regression, which is a decent sign it works.

VERIFICATION: full test:all green — 337 + 20 unit, 266 parity (0 failed, 0 skipped), 45 goldens, 118 cases match the oracle inventory, 30/30 oracle mutations, test:pure 261 tests 0 skipped, allowlist coverage 5/5 ids witnessed by the mechanism each declares.
title: Allowlist IDs asserted by NON-CASE tests have no execution evidence
